articles.title: Apple HomeView : le nouvel écran domotique est-il déjà obsolète en 2026 ? — Frandroid
articles.text:
C’est un lancement un peu surprenant pour Apple. En début de semaine dernière, la firme à la pomme a présenté son HomeView, un écran connecté destiné à prendre le contrôle sur votre installation domotique. S’il s’agit d’une nouvelle catégorie de produits pour la marque, on ne peut pas dire que l’appareil impressionne par son design ou sa fiche technique.
Les imposantes bordures autour de l’écran, la puce A18, les huit gigas de RAM. Rien de tout ça ne semble révolutionnaire fin 2026. Et pour cause, selon Mark Gurman, le produit aurait dû sortir bien avant, mais « a dormi dans un entrepôt pendant presque un an ».
Du retard à l’allumage
L’aspect matériel de l’appareil aurait été fini bien avant que le logiciel ne le soit et l’écran aurait donc pris la poussière le temps qu’Apple daigne lui offrir un système d’exploitation digne de ce nom. Comme les rumeurs l’évoquaient déjà depuis 2024, ce sont les ratés de la firme dans le secteur de l’intelligence artificielle qui ont causé du retard dans la sortie du produit. Résultat, un projet imaginé début 2023 a fini par sortir fin 2026 avec une fiche technique de mi 2024.
Bloomberg en veut pour preuve que certains anciens employés d’Apple ont évoqué leur implication dans la conception du produit malgré le fait qu’ils ne travaillent plus pour la firme depuis un long moment. Carl Schoeller fait partie de ceux-là malgré le fait que son passage chez Apple se soit terminé en septembre 2023.
Cela explique aussi pourquoi Apple s’est allié avec LG pour le lancement de sa gamme de produits domotiques. Il y a un an et quelques, la firme n’avait pas la triste réputation qu’elle a aujourd’hui dans le domaine de la vie privée et sans doute qu’une collaboration paraissait opportune. Aujourd’hui, cela paraît plus difficile à justifier.
Un HomeView Max pour bientôt ?
Soyons honnêtes, cela dit, un écran connecté n’a nullement besoin d’arborer une fiche technique révolutionnaire, surtout quand ce dernier n’a vocation qu’à servir d’interface pour Siri et éventuellement de machine à passer des appels FaceTime. Cela ne devrait, cela dit, pas empêcher Apple de sortir une autre version très bientôt.
    Pour aller plus loin
Toutes les annonces Apple « Welcome home » : Apple HomeView, Apple TV 4K (2026) et HomePod mini 2
            
Toujours d’après Bloomberg, un HomeView Max/Ultra pourrait bien sortir en 2027/2028. Ce dernier arborerait un écran de neuf pouces et un pied pivotant à 360° permettant à l’appareil de suivre les mouvements du propriétaire ou de cadrer la personne qui parle lors d’un appel FaceTime grâce à la reconnaissance vocale. Une idée plus intéressante que ce qu’Apple propose aujourd’hui.

articles.title: Europa quiere hacer algo que parecía imposible y es comprar energía como si fuera un solo país
articles.text:
La Unión Europea está buscando nuevas formas de hacer frente a un mercado cada vez más volátil y menos fiable. En esta ocasión, es la presidenta de la Comisión Úrsula Von der Leyen quien presenta estos días ante el Parlamento Europeo una propuesta inédita: agregar toda la demanda del continente y hacer compras conjuntas de energía. Como si fuéramos un solo país.
100.000 millones de euros de más. Eso es lo que hemos pagado los europeos por los combustibles fósiles importados desde el inicio de la guerra de Irán, según las declaraciones de la presidenta de la Comisión Europea que recoge la Agencia EFE.
Esto se debe al encarecimiento de la energía, más concretamente del gas, que ha aumentado un 140%, y de los precios de los carburantes, a pesar de la liberación de 100 millones de barriles de diésel y crudo por parte del G7. Todo ha inflado la factura energética en esa cantidad millonaria sin que haya supuesto recibir «una molécula adicional de energía».
¿La unión hace la fuerza? Para hacer frente a esta situación crítica, al menos en el corto plazo, Von der Leyen propone dar un paso más en el modelo que utilizó Europa en la anterior crisis de 2022, cuando puso en contacto a compradores y vendedores de gas para intentar salir del paso. Ahora, lo que sugiere es que la Unión Europea agregue la demanda de sus Estados miembro y pueda negociar así una compra conjunta de la energía que necesita, centralizando la contratación y coordinando los esfuerzos del continente. Concretamente, el plan contempla, además del gas, compras de petróleo, de hidrógeno verde y de los minerales críticos necesarios para el desarrollo de baterías.
Con esto, se evitaría que hubiese 27 negociaciones para 27 contratos distintos de cada uno de los 27 países que conforman la Unión y se podría utilizar esta actuación en bloque como presión para conseguir mejores acuerdos, en un momento en el que el mercado energético está disparado.
Pero esto no resuelve el problema. Von der Leyen ha sido clara y ha compartido que a medio y largo plazo la solución debe ser la electrificación de la economía europea. Para la jefa del Ejecutivo comunitario, solo atajando los problemas estructurales que existen a nivel energético, como la dependencia energética del continente, se podrá reducir la exposición de la economía europea a las perturbaciones internacionales.
Y es que, a pesar de las medidas que se tomen, estas perturbaciones pueden mantenerse o empeorar este invierno, ya que Europa afronta el frío con las reservas gasísticas más bajas de su historia reciente.
Urge soberanía energética. El plan de Von der Leyen pasa por que la Unión Europea refuerce su autonomía estratégica, sobre todo, a través de las renovables. Como explican desde El Independiente, Europa aún sigue apoyándose en el gas, el petróleo y los combustibles tradicionales para gran parte de su mix energético. De ahí que las metas sean pasar del 23% al 46% de electrificación en 2040. Con este objetivo, las economías europeas podrían ahorrarse hasta 260.000 millones de euros anuales en compras energéticas a terceros.
Imagen | François Genon
En Xataka | El mapa energético está cambiando: ya no gana quien tiene más gas, sino quien puede sacarlo al mercado

articles.title: Intel Core i5-4670K Gets a New Cinebench R11.5 Record, 13 Years After Launch
articles.text:
Sunday, October 18th 2026
Intel Core i5-4670K Gets a New Cinebench R11.5 Record, 13 Years After Launch
Overclocker Luumi has taken the top spot in HWBot's Cinebench R11.5 rankings for the Intel Core i5-4670K, beating a record that had stood for around 12 years. Running the 2013 Haswell quad-core at 6,301 MHz under liquid nitrogen, Luumi scored 10.8 cb, just edging out Strat's previous 10.76 cb at 6,249 MHz. That's roughly 66% above the chip's 3.8 GHz boost clock, which is quite a lot for a four-core, four-thread part built on Intel's 22 nm process. The top of the leaderboard is tight as well, with Moose83 sitting third at 10.74 cb out of 187 submissions. Of course, this is a record for the i5-4670K category, not an overall Cinebench R11.5 world record. Luumi also has a history with Cinebench, having set an 8-core world record on an EVGA Z390 Dark back in 2018.
The test bench was period-correct too. Luumi used an ASRock Z97 OC Formula, the same board that pushed a Core i7-4790K past 7 GHz back in 2014, along with 4 GB of XPG DDR3 running at 2,708 MT/s with 8-12-7-28 timings and a Corsair AXi 1600 power supply. The run was done on Windows 7, as HWBot's R11.5 rules apparently don't allow pre-Skylake Intel chips on newer versions of Windows without BenchMate. Haswell is no stranger to extreme clocks, as the Core i7-4770K was overclocked to 7 GHz before it even launched in 2013. A modern 12-core laptop reportedly scores around four times higher in R11.5 while running in quiet mode, so the achievement here is about squeezing every last megahertz out of 13-year-old silicon.
Sources:
				HWBot, 				via Wccftech

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang explains why the new Surface Laptop Ultra is "really a work of love"
articles.text:
'This computer is going to be incredible': Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang explains why the new Surface Laptop Ultra is "really a work of love"
Nvidia CEO sings the praises of the new Surface Laptop Ultra
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has sung the praises of Microsoft's new Surface Laptop Ultra, describing it as "so beautiful" and "incredible".
Speaking at a developer event in London, Huang outlined the development process that went into building the hardware powering the new product, which is the first Microsoft device powered by an Nvidia chip.
“This computer is going to be incredible - it took us four years to build it," Huang told attendees including TechRadar Pro, "this project is really a work of love - we had several thousand engineering years dedicated to it, we build a brand new revolutionary chip, a whole new line of PCs, it’s so beautiful - you’re going to love it.”
The end of the traditional PC?
Revealed in September 2026, the Surface Laptop Ultra is targeted towards developer and AI usage, powered by Nvidia’s RTX Spark platform with an N1X processor and RTX Blackwell graphics, supporting up to 128GB unified memory
This is alongside 24GB RAM and 512GB storage, while the next version has 32GB RAM and 1TB storage, making it ideal for creators, AI specialists, engineers, scientists, developers, and other users running demanding applications.
But as Huang tells it, the creation of the device, set to launch on October 16 2026, was a long and arduous process.
“It took four years to do this," Huang said of the hardware development process. "We were thinking about agentic systems, AI and autonomous systems, and how they’ll be able to access your files, and be grounded on information, and be able to reason about it and use tools - but the ultimate tool is your personal computer, right?"
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
"So wouldn’t it be cool if we could create a personal computer, a PC that actually runs an agent locally - so it can go off and just work on things for you - and not only could it just run locally, it would be smart enough to use the tools."
Huang explained his vision of "texting" your PC to ask for help, to get it to do tasks like rendering images and updating slides, then delivering them straight to you.
"Wouldn’t it be awesome if you could just text your computer - you don’t have to bring it with you anymore - just leave it at your desk!”
“So we created this thing - it took us four years to do it, so I called Satya (Nadella, Microsoft CEO), and the two of us talked about it…and so we had to create a brand new chip, we had to wait until Blackwell was done - and this thing has 1 petaflops of computing, and because we knew the models were going to be big, we had to redesign how the GPU uses memory - so this is the first Nvidia GPU with shared memory, one petaflops, Blackwell architecture - and also it has to run everything a PC doesn’t.”
“There’s three types of PCs, right," Huang outlined, "there’s the PC that basically you use to type in - that’s called a PC, there’s the Nvidia gaming PC, you’ve got GeForce in that, and you’ve got the Nvidia workstations that runs all kinds of applications…so we figured that if you’re going to have an AI go use the tools, it should be able to use every single tool…it runs everything, it runs every AI framework, it runs any AI model as well."

He has worked as a B2B and B2C tech journalist for over a decade, including at one of the UK's leading national newspapers and fellow Future title ITProPortal. articles.title: No agenda, no rush, no leaving San Francisco: Benchmark’s partners on investing in a frenzied market | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The players sometimes change. I sat down with four of Benchmark’s partners three years ago, and three of those individuals are no longer with the firm. The capital commitments have changed, too. This summer, Benchmark announced $2 billion across two funds, marking only the second time in its 31-year history that it has veered from raising a far smaller vehicle.
But at this week’s TechCrunch Disrupt, the venture firm’s five partners convincingly portrayed a close-knit team that’s not about to put the pedal to the metal, even as many of their rivals do exactly that. The world may be speeding up, but they’re investing at the pace Benchmark always has: just two or three new bets per year per partner. The world is drowning in information, yet their Monday partner meetings still have no agenda. And while economic indicators point to trouble ahead, they don’t seem too bothered, seeing many of the warning signs as products of X-fueled hysteria.
Here’s what Benchmark’s five general partners — gathered together on our stage — had to say at the show. Some of the comments below have been edited for length and clarity; you can watch the full interview at the end of the article.
Benchmark has evolved in some ways, including a bigger core fund and a new growth fund. How do you think about adapting without losing what makes you Benchmark?
Peter Fenton: The craft that hasn’t changed is the core fund: working closely with founders at the beginning. It’s usually a 10-to-15-year commitment, [working] shoulder to shoulder, and that doesn’t scale. There’s also been inflation. We held the core fund at $500 million for 20 years, and it has just inflated to be consistent with the existing economy, which we hadn’t done and that was probably a tactical error on our part.
[As for the growth fund] it’s an expansion of our mandate. In some ways, we get permission from the ecosystem to do more than just the core early-stage business. [Not having this previously] was a fork in our eye. A number of opportunities that came to Benchmark would have returned somewhere between 10 and 1,000x to Benchmark, and we were constricted by our early-stage focus.
Are you thinking to make handful of bets with that $1.25 billion growth fund?
Fenton: We all have different answers, which is the beauty of a partnership. I’d love for us to have, as that great J.P. Morgan paper puts it, the agony and ecstasy of a concentrated portfolio. If the fund is successful, one or two investments will generate 90% of the returns. So I think it’s four to six, maybe seven to eight.
Ev, you joined Benchmark late last year. You’ve worked at Founders Fund, Bond, and Kleiner Perkins. How does Benchmark differ?
Ev Randall: Every firm is ultimately a collection of the people within the firm and how they work together. Some are very hierarchical, with a 50- or 60-person investment team and investment processes that are federated into product groups. And then you have small partnerships. Very early in my career, I was drawn to small partnerships because they allow a higher level of throughput and fidelity in your conversations, where you don’t feel like you’re making decisions through some Byzantine corporate structure. You’re going out on the field together, like a sports team.
And then the other piece is: You have to find your people, You have to find people who you not only like but admire. With Benchmark, with the current crop of GPs, it was obvious that everyone liked each other and got along, but it went deeper than that. It’s a group that admires each other and learns from each other. That mix of attributes is very rare, and when I saw it, I immediately wanted to join, and I think Jack felt the same way also as a newcomer.
Jack, you joined in February, but it was just a year ago that you raised a second, $275 million fund for your own firm in what you told the Wall Street Journal took one week. You have a hugely popular podcast. Why join Benchmark?
Jack Altman: It’s funny. I did the podcast with these guys at the start of this year, and during that podcast, obviously we talked about the commitment to being a small fund, but more than that, what I heard was that they want to be the first people who founders call, they want to be concentrated, and they just care. So much in this industry gets tied up in money and status, and what I felt from the Benchmark team then, and ten times more as I’ve gotten to know them so well, is it’s a group that really cares about founders and helping companies. And I did enjoy being an individual investor. . .but in a market this crazy, I don’t know how I’d feel, figuring it out on my own. Having a group of people who are so smart and focused and driven to learn it with and from has been awesome. There’s no better place to learn.
I’m told you meet on Mondays with no agenda.
Chethan Puttagunta: Jack tried to make an agenda. [Laughs.]
Altman: I’ve got an agenda for next Monday.
Eric Vishria: It’s weirdly arbitrary, honestly. It’s an ongoing conversation. In a time of rapid change, you’re trying to figure out what’s becoming possible that wasn’t possible six months ago, and who’s bending light. We talk about what companies we’re meeting, what piqued our interest and why, what we’re seeing in board meetings. You can try to systematize it, but one of the beauties of five people is you don’t have to. It’s a decades-long conversation that only works if you’re small and actually enjoy spending time together. After this session, we’re having dinner with one of the very few entrepreneurs who has built a multi-hundred-billion-dollar company, someone we’re not invested in, just to stretch our thinking.
Puttagunta: Part of not having an agenda is you need space to be reactive. If a founder needs help landing an executive or a strategic partnership, the five of us can be at their disposal.
You’re an equal partnership. Can one person put the kibosh on a deal?
Puttagunta: Nobody knows. We don’t have rules around it.
Altman: I actually don’t know. I was waiting to see what someone else [said].
It’s never happened?
Altman: Because the firm is structured around a low volume of deals, you don’t actually want to have all of this rigor. If we invested in 100 or 200 companies a year, you’d want a CRM and a formal voting process. Because it’s so rare, the lack of structure is a huge asset.
Fenton: One of the differentiating aspects of our brand is we’re not so cocksure to come in and say ‘winner’ or ‘loser.’ It’s not Shark Tank. We sort of feel awe, for lack of a better term, at all the possibilities . . . The occasional case where someone comes in who’s polarizing — the entrepreneurs feel that. If someone in the room doesn’t like you, we’re not a great partner.
Companies are growing faster than ever. I’d think it’s easier to feel you’re missing out on opportunities if you don’t invest with greater frequency. Have you picked up the pace?
Puttagunta: I think the pace is consistent. I think part of the reality of venture capital in our business is that we are not going to be part of every successful company, and that’s okay. There are companies that we identify, we find that the entrepreneur has some great strength, and we want to amplify that strength. And it’s our job to find a way to work with that person. It kind of doesn’t matter how much capital they want to raise, or what structure, or where they are. You just have to work through all that stuff.
One thing that founders are interested in as a trend is VCs backing competing companies. Has that VC-founder pact changed because companies are growing so quickly and expanding into one another’s territory?
Vishria: One of the things we have an ethos around is, we are making a commitment to an entrepreneur, and through that commitment, we’re saying we’re going to work with you in this thing, and whatever that thing is, and we are working closely enough where it matters, and it should matter to them, and as it matters to us. The harsh reality of this world is every company is evolving very quickly, and so you do have companies that will naturally evolve from one thing to another, or pivot or change, and you are going to get conflicts. That’s just the reality of the of the kind of current dynamic. . .
Of course, we’re maintaining confidentiality and doing those things and fortunate to not end up in in that type of insane direct conflict [as happened recently with rival companies Factory and Cognition]. . . that commitment of exclusivity in that area is really important. But things are evolving. There’s no doubt about that.
Puttagunta: And I think people are ultra ambitious in this AI era. As the cost of coding new products effectively goes to zero, founders see a surface area and they want to attack the surface area, and so I think it’s probably going to happen more, where you start to run into each other. But there’s a way to be there’s a way to maintain that relationship and be respectful.
Jack, have you made an investment for Benchmark yet, and if so, did you feel a lot of pressure with that first deal?
Altman: I have, a few, and some are recent, so not all are disclosed. My background was software, but since joining, I’ve done chips, robotics and infra. Someone asked me when I joined, ‘How was the onboarding?’ And I was like, ‘It was perfect. There was no onboarding.’ Either Chethan or Eric told me early on, ‘Hey, you’re going to feel tight on your first one. Don’t. You’re going to make many investments while you’re here. This whole game includes crazy power laws. The odds of it being your first are low.’ . . . I trusted they understood what my shape was as a person, as an investor, and I was going to just try to stay as consistent to that as I could.
It really is a group dynamic on a lot of these. The investments I’ve made, I don’t think we would have won them if I didn’t have my partners. I don’t know that I would have been able to know how to get to a yes without them.
Eric, the AI chip company Cerebras was an unusual bet for Benchmark at the time it was made. What persuaded you to move forward with it?
Vishria: We invested in the spring of 2016, in the first round. We hadn’t made a hardware investment in 10 years. The founders seemed good, they had a very simple thesis, and I didn’t understand most of the rest. On the Sunday night before they came back to pitch the partnership, Peter told me it went against everything he’d learned in venture. Then, after the Monday pitch, he had flipped. A big part of it is understanding each other’s instincts. That began a journey of lots of ups and downs and many potential deaths of the company along the way, and it’s far from over. The romanticism of falling in love with a founder and an idea is why we do this.
Fenton: Andrew and his co-founders are heretics. What they were saying was unorthodox, and you see it today, with people dumping on the stock because it’s polarizing. That’s exactly where we have to be as investors. If it’s consensus, why is there a startup?
On that point, Cerebras priced at $185 when it went public earlier this year, jumped to $350, and is back near $185. Why?
Vishria: About six weeks before the IPO, I showed the company stock chart after stock chart: CoreWeave, Datadog, DoorDash, Amazon. Peak to trough, it’s insane how many of them move 500% in a year, up and down. So who knows? You control what you can control, and you update the public markets every 12 weeks. Being a public company takes a stomach of titanium, and the employees have to understand that.
Your former colleague, Bill Gurley, long argued that the traditional IPO process is broken, that that IPO ‘pop’ benefits bankers and their clients — not the company. He’s a proponent of direct listings. Does anyone here agree with that thinking?
Vishria: I think maybe of this group, I’m the only one who’s worked on a direct listing. It can for sure make sense. I think the reality is for this crop of AI companies, it’s going to be unlikely because they need capital, and they need a lot of capital. At the end of the day, IPOs raise money. Cerebras raised $6 billion. That matters, so I think it’s probably unlikely for this crop just because most of them need capital.
Could a severe correction be coming? A lot of AI companies have exhausted their free cash flow. It’s very expensive for companies to borrow. We also just saw the first AI bankruptcy with Character AI.
Randall: Macro is always a fool’s errand to predict with precision. What has changed most since I started investing is the information environment. Character.AI was the leftover corpse of a company whose founder and team were acqui-hired into Google a year and a half ago, and it was already sold for $2.3 billion; its Chapter 11 being read as an AI chill effect shows that the info environment for public equities in tech has been drawn so much into this, like, hyperactive X echo chamber.
If you look at the market today and you see where CoreWeave and Nebius and all these things are trading, those numbers are are due to the ARR figures of two private companies that will probably be public in the next 12 months . . .There’s so much capex and there’s so much investment that runs through the estimated and projected health of OpenAI and Anthropic.
Our companies see so much demand that they can’t get enough compute to serve customers who are willing to pay them at good gross margins. There’s nothing inherently unhealthy about the AI ecosystem. What’s unhealthy is the volatility from data points that are often untrue or exaggerated for clicks. I do think OpenAI and Anthropic going public would be healthy, so the market stops swinging 5% to 10% every time an anonymous account updates an estimate.
Those two companies have also really pulled the center of gravity back to San Francisco. Do you have to be in San Francisco to be a founder now? Are you interested in companies outside of California?
Altman: I don’t know that you have to be here as a founder, but I think it is right now by far the easiest place to get talent, capital, and customers. Probably everyone [on the team] works with companies that are not in San Francisco, but we’re also here in San Francisco every day, so I wouldn’t say you have to, but I’d say: strong bias for our particular setup.
Fenton: Historically, 90%-plus percent of the capital returns have come from companies founded here. There are beautiful stories outside that dense probability distribution — Shopify is a great example, Ramp — but the ecosystem effect that occurs when you have a successful company and that leads to a background of great executives [and] ambitious people, the bar of success gets raised. I don’t think it has systemically happened anywhere quite like here.
Randall: I’m trying to think of a non-SF based company that I’ve met with in the last 18 months that wasn’t actively saying that they were spending time in San Francisco. They’ve either opening an office in San Francisco, they’re spending half of their time in San Francisco, or they’re planning to move out to San Francisco. Iron sharpens iron. If you want to be around peers who are going to make you the best version of yourself, and it’s hard to think of a city that does that better than San Francisco in the current era that we’re in now with AI here.

articles.title: KI kann uns falsche Erinnerungen einreden
articles.text:
MIT-Forscherin warnt: KI könnte bei Menschen falsche Erinnerungen erzeugen
Einer im Frühjahr 2026 veröffentlichten Studie zufolge vertrauen Menschen KI-generierten Antworten oft zu schnell und überschätzen die Kompetenz von KI-Systemen. Die Forscher:innen kamen zu dem Schluss, dass Menschen zu viel Vertrauen in KI-Empfehlungen setzen könnten, selbst wenn das System unsicher oder fehleranfällig sei.
Falsche Erinnerungen durch KI
Ein aktuelles Experiment der MIT-Forscherin Pattie Maes schlägt in eine ähnliche Kerbe. Demnach könnten KI-Systeme bei Menschen falsche Erinnerungen erzeugen, wie die Professorin vom MIT Media Lab gegenüber der Washington Post erklärte.
Im Rahmen des Experiments zeigten Maes und ihr Team 200 Teilnehmer:innen 24 Fotos. Auf diesen waren etwa eine Hochzeit, eine Straßenszene oder ein Rennen zu sehen. Anschließend bekam ein Teil der Gruppe dieselben Bilder noch einmal zu sehen. Für die anderen hatten die Forscher:innen von KI veränderte Versionen parat.
Gedächtnistest zeigt Gefahr
Dort waren etwa die Gesichtsausdrücke verändert oder Militärpersonal hinzugefügt worden, wie fr.de schreibt. Auch hatte die KI wohl Hinweise zum Klimawandel ergänzt. Bei dem folgenden Gedächtnistest zeigte sich, dass bei denjenigen, die von der KI veränderte Fotos zu sehen bekamen, die Zahl der falschen Erinnerungen stieg.
Und das war noch nicht alles. Die betroffenen Teilnehmer:innen waren von diesen falschen Erinnerungen auch noch überzeugter. „Ich halte das alles für grundsätzlich sehr gefährlich“, so Maes.
Gerichte und Geschichte manipulierbar?
Die Forscher:in spielt damit unter anderem auf Gerichtsverfahren an, bei denen Richter:innen auf möglichst korrekte Erinnerungen angewiesen sind. Schon jetzt ist klar, dass Erinnerungen von Zeug:innen leicht verzerrbar sind. Und auch die Geschichtsschreibung hängt von Erinnerungen ab.
Auf einer KI-Konferenz im schwedischen Malmö sind Forscher:innen Mitte Oktober 2026 der Frage nachgegangen, was passiert, wenn KI beginnt, sich in das menschliche Gedächtnis einzumischen. Nicht nur Maes Forschungsarbeit, sondern weitere Studien deuten daraufhin, dass KI verzerren kann, woran Menschen sich erinnern.
KI-Ideen versus menschliche Gedanken
In einem Fall etwa sahen die Teilnehmer:innen ein Video über ein Verbrechen. Diejenigen, die dazu später von einem generativen KI-Chatbot befragt wurden, hatten dreimal so viele falsche Erinnerungen. Auch die Grenzen zwischen den eigenen Gedanken und jenen von Maschinen scheinen zu verwischen. Ganz zu schweigen davon, dass Erinnerungen an Ereignisse eingepflanzt werden könnten, die es nie gab.

articles.title: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’ | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Anthropic announced today that it’s creating a “public benefit fund” that will give the company “increased flexibility and scale” to support projects for societal good.
Anthropic said that it will commit 5% of its shares to the fund — structured as a wholly-owned entity within the company — with the option to contribute an additional 2% for every 50% increase in Anthropic’s value. And it offered some broad-strokes ideas for how this money might actually be used, such as “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.”
There’s also the impact that AI might have on the job market, which Anthropic has already committed $200 million to study. But the company said, “Given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.”
Anthropic’s announcement comes as the AI industry faces increasingly negative public sentiment, which CEO Dario Amodei has described as “fundamentally a crisis of trust.”
If you’re wondering who will actually decide which public benefits are worth funding, Anthropic said it will share more information about structure and governance in the coming months.

articles.title: F-22 Raptor pilot successfully demonstrates command of 'wingman' fighter drone in simulated combat — Anduril YFQ-44A Fury test advances USAF’s program to integrate uncrewed aircraft into fighter squadrons
articles.text:
F-22 Raptor pilot successfully demonstrates command of 'wingman' fighter drone in simulated combat — Anduril YFQ-44A Fury test advances USAF’s program to integrate uncrewed aircraft into fighter squadrons
One more step into the future of air combat.
The U.S. Air Force has just successfully conducted an airborne test where an F-22 Raptor pilot directed an Anduril YFQ-44A Fury drone during simulated combat. According to The Defense Watch, the fighter pilot gave tactical commands to the autonomous wingman, which then interpreted them into a series of tasks and flight maneuvers to achieve the desired outcome.
The successful test is part of the USAF’s Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), which seeks to integrate drones into fighter squadrons. These uncrewed aircraft must be able to respond to the fighter pilot’s tactical commands and then operate autonomously, though. That’s because fighter pilots already have a heavy workload — flying their own aircraft, managing sensor data, threat assessment, and weapons release decisions — so requiring them to manually fly a drone is next to impossible. Command integration means that the F-22 Raptor pilot could assign the Fury drone a specific tactical task, like monitoring for and engaging enemy air defenses, while they focus on the primary mission, such as taking out enemy fighters.
This does not mean that the USAF can start deploying drones alongside fighter jets in frontline squadrons, though. Successful command integration is just the first of several hurdles that the program must go through before it can achieve operational status. The program needs to determine the limits of the drone’s tactical autonomy, safe flight control, and weapons authorization, all of which are separate functions that must be tested accordingly. The Air Force also needs to see how the drone performs with electronic interference, and how it could continuously operate if it cannot receive instructions due to interrupted communications. Aside from figuring out the drone’s capabilities and incorporating it into fighter doctrine, it must also be integrated into the USAF’s logistics and supply chain. This includes drone maintenance and service, weapons handling, deployment procedures, and forward airbase operations with limited infrastructure.
Even though the latest test is seemingly successful, the CCA still needs to go a long way before it can start operational deployment. Nevertheless, the USAF is intent on pushing the project forward, as it sees autonomous drones as a force multiplier for crewed aircraft, allowing a single pilot to command multiple jets to achieve missions at a lower cost compared to using all-crewed aircraft. Other nations, like Sweden and China, are also experimenting with a similar concept of having a single operator take command of multiple drones, but the most significant difference of the CCA is that it focuses on air power instead of ground-based operations.

articles.title: Top 10 videos más vistos en YouTube España hoy
articles.text:
YouTube ha adquirido una importancia sin precedentes en el mundo moderno y en su momento se convirtió en un fenómeno que llegó a revolucionar la forma en que se consume el contenido audiovisual.
Antes de su existencia el acceso a este tipo de clips estaba limitado a canales de televisión tradicionales y producciones de gran presupuesto, sin embargo, YouTube ha permitido que cualquier persona con una cámara y una conexión a internet pueda hacer y compartir sus propios clips, lo que ha beneficiado a la aparición de una amplia cantidad de canales que brindan desde contenido educativo hasta de entretenimiento.
La plataforma también ha funcionado como un trampolín para artistas emergentes, músicos, comediantes y cineastas independientes, quienes han encontrado en YouTube una audiencia global y la posibilidad de obtener reconocimiento sin pasar por los canales tradicionales de la industria del entretenimiento.
YouTube tiene presencia en 104 países y está disponible en 80 idiomas, lo que la ha llevado a convertirse en la biblioteca digital de videos más grande y prueba de ello es que a ella se suben más de 500 horas de contenido cada minuto, al día son vistos 5 mil millones de videos y las ganancias se estiman en 15 mil millones de dólares al trimestre.
Ante estas cifras podría ser un tanto difícil perderse las novedades o los clips que están siendo los más populares, es por eso que YouTube cuenta desde 2018 con diversas listas en donde se pueden consultar los artistas más escuchados, los videos más vistos y cuáles son las tendencias del día en tiempo real.
Aquí el listado de los 10 videos que están en tendencia en YouTube España
1. Bulin 47 X Kevin Wai - Dame Hombro (Video Oficial)Artista/canal: Bulin 47 Oficial
2. VuelveArtista/canal: Anuel AA
3. Judeline - La Falda (Official Video)Artista/canal: Judeline
4. JukiarArtista/canal: Quevedo y Clarent
5. PARADIXEArtista/canal: Pirlo, El Americano 4KT y Feid
6. RETRICAArtista/canal: Lucho RK
7. Olivia Rodrigo - expectations (feat. Chappell Roan) (Official Music Video)Artista/canal: Olivia Rodrigo
8. Bicho raroArtista/canal: Estopa
9. 0 AMIGOS cap. 5 - YOLAMASCARAArtista/canal: YOLAMASCARA
10. Miki Núñez, The Tyets - Raquel Sans (Official)Artista/canal: Miki Núñez
El éxito de YouTube
YouTube vio la luz en febrero de 2005, cuando tres antiguos empleados de la compañía de Paypal ―Chad Hurley, Steve Chen y Jawed Karim― se unieron y la crearon luego de que experimentaran dificultades para compartir entre sí un par de videos tras asistir a una fiesta.
El dominio fue activado el 14 de febrero de 2005 y casi un mes después, el 23 de abril, fue cargado el primer clip a la plataforma que llevaba por nombre “Me at the Zoo”. Fue cuestión de tiempo para que todo el mundo comenzara a cargar contenido y a compartir los enlaces a través de otras redes sociales como MySpace.
Una de las grandes empresas que vio el potencial de YouTube fue la marca Nike, que subió una publicidad protagonizada por Ronaldinho, lo que hizo que otras grandes compañías voltearan a ver a YouTube y se sintieran atraídas.
Tal fue la gran acogida de los internautas por YouTube que para diciembre de 2005 la plataforma pasó de las 50 millones de visitas al día a 250 millones de visualizaciones luego de que un canal subiera el clip musical Lazy Sunday, transmitido originalmente por Saturday Night Live.
Para el año siguiente, en el 2006, el sitio fue comparado por el gigante del internet, Google, por un valor de 1650 millones de dólares. En ese entonces eran visualizados 100 millones de videos al día y 65 mil clips se añadían a diario. También firmaron acuerdos con disqueras para poder reproducir videos musicales.
Las polémicas de YouTube
Desde que fue puesto en marcha, YouTube fue un sitio que llegó a hacer una revolución no sólo en internet, sino también en la forma en la que los usuarios miran contenido. Muestra de ello el reconocimiento que la revista Time le otorgó en noviembre del 2006 al ser nombrado el “Invento del Año”.
Convertido en el mejor medio de difusión, el gozar de tanta popularidad también ha metido a sus dueños en aprietos como cuando albergar peleas escolares o en donde hay bullying, clips relacionados al terrorismo, narcotráfico u otros temas considerados delicados por su contenido íntimo o por mostrar delitos como asesinatos y más.
Para Estados Unidos uno de los temas más delicados es el de los tiroteos escolares, por lo que YouTube ha estado más de una vez en el ojo del huracán por alojar contenido filmado por los atacantes, como fue el caso de la masacre de Virginia Tech, cuando Cho Seung-Hui, el atacante, subió previamente a los hechos un discurso.
Más recientemente, tras el surgimiento de la pandemia del coronavirus, también ha surgido inquietud sobre cómo la plataforma permite la monetización de contenido que puede ser engañoso y riesgoso para la población.
Aunque no todo es malo, pues a través de dicha plataforma muchas personas han podido ser reconocidas por su talento, como fue el caso de Susan Boyle, quien participó en el programa Britain’s Got Talent cuyo extracto subido a YouTube logró que la mujer pasara a ser una completa desconocida a una de las personas más viralizadas, famosas y aclamadas del internet.

articles.title: How art platforms, exhibitions and awards strengthen the creative economy
articles.text:
How art platforms, exhibitions and awards strengthen the creative economy
In this photo essay from Lalit Kala Akademi in New Delhi, we showcase more highlights from an exhibition with 270 artworks from across India.
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,020 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.
Lalit Kala Akademi (LKA) in New Delhi recently hosted its 65th National Exhibition of Art. It showcased over 270 artworks from around the country, selected by a jury from 6,175 submissions.
Twenty artists were also conferred with the Lalit Kala Akademi Awards. The artists include Pooja Rajpoot, Praveen Kumar, Pritam Madhukar Deuskar, Rajendra Prasad, Ramesh Vithal Thorat, Raviram Ramakrishnan, and Sanjay Kumar.
Such exhibitions and awards help transform artistic talent into livelihoods, creative businesses, tourism, and international recognition. By connecting artists with audiences, buyers, institutions, and markets, they strengthen the creative economy while preserving a country’s cultural identity.
Exhibitions provide artists with platforms to showcase, promote and sell their work. They connect creators with the broader ecosystem of collectors, galleries, curators, cultural institutions and potential investors, thus creating opportunities for income generation and professional growth.
In the case of national exhibitions in India, opportunities are also created to showcase traditional crafts, indigenous knowledge, and contemporary artistic practices. Cultural assets thus go beyond elements of nostalgia into sources of sustainable economic value.
Art competitions in turn encourage excellence, experimentation and creative risk-taking. When conducted annually, they identify emerging talent, provide visibility to underrepresented artists, and create pathways to grants and residencies, as shown in LKA's activities and centres across India.
Art exhibitions delight and inspire art lovers while also spurring artists to develop new techniques, materials and ideas. At a broader level, this strengthens a country’s creative skills base and encourage innovation across design, fashion, architecture, digital media, and other creative industries.
Awards conferred by national institutions like LKA provide credibility and elevate the profiles of artists and creative enterprises. National awards also help establish benchmarks of excellence, celebrate cultural achievement, and build a distinctive national creative identity.
As shown in this photo essay, the diverse artworks featured help emerging artists realise what is possible with current practices. It also opens the door to explore how other media can extend creative frontiers, such as digital technologies.
Together, exhibitions, competitions and awards contribute to the creative economy of India. Regional creators can connect to national and international buyers, galleries, cultural institutions, and digital marketplaces.
Traditional art forms and indigenous knowledge can be sustained while encouraging new creative expressions. The LKA annual exhibition encourages cultural institutions and private-sector partners to invest in accessible venues, professional development, and fair artist remuneration.
Particular attention should be given to emerging artists, regional creative communities, women, youth, and indigenous practitioners. Success should be measured not only by attendance or media coverage, but also by artist earnings, tourism spending, repeat market opportunities, and international partnerships.
In sum, sustained investment and effective partnerships via platforms like LKA can ensure that India’s artistic and cultural wealth generates lasting social, cultural and economic value.
Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world?
(All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location at Lalit Kala Akademi.)

articles.title: Votre connexion Wi-Fi ralentit tous les jours à la même heure, et vos voisins en sont peut-être la cause
articles.text:
Votre connexion Wi-Fi ralentit tous les jours à la même heure, et vos voisins en sont peut-être la cause
Si votre connexion Wi-Fi ralentit tous les jours à la même heure, ce n’est pas forcément à cause de votre box. Et pour cause, vos voisins sont peut-être la cause de ce ralentissement.
En général, c’est le soir qu’une connexion Wi-Fi ralentit, quand tous les foyers sont au complet et se connectent en masse pour regarder Netflix, jouer en ligne, télécharger des fichiers ou passer des appels vidéo. Dans un immeuble ou un quartier, cette hausse de l’activité encombre parfois les fréquences utilisées par les réseaux Wi-Fi à proximité, voire une partie du réseau de l’opérateur. Autrement dit, vos voisins n’ont pas besoin d’être connectés à votre box pour ralentir votre Wi-Fi : leurs propres réseaux utilisent parfois les mêmes fréquences que le vôtre.
Pourquoi vos voisins peuvent ralentir votre Wi-Fi ?
Tout d’abord, séparons deux choses : le Wi-Fi est la liaison radio entre votre smartphone, votre PC ou votre téléviseur et votre box.
L’accès à Internet est la connexion que votre opérateur, comme Orange, Free, SFR ou Bouygues Telecom, donne à votre box. Un ralentissement peut donc apparaître chez vous même si Internet fonctionne parfaitement.
Le problème le plus fréquent touche la bande de 2,4 GHz. Il s’agit d’une fréquence qui porte plus loin et traverse mieux les murs, mais beaucoup de box et d’appareils connectés l’utilisent.
Dans un immeuble, plusieurs réseaux proches émettent parfois sur le même canal. Si les box de vos voisins utilisent le même canal que le vôtre, tous ces réseaux se partagent le temps disponible pour transmettre leurs données.
Quand beaucoup de réseaux choisissent le même canal, qui est une petite portion de fréquence utilisée par la box pour communiquer avec les appareils connectés, ils attendent alors leur tour pour transmettre des données.
Ce qui explique ce ralentissement de la connexion Wi-Fi, généralement en soirée. Quand les réseaux voisins sont actifs au même moment, l'attente augmente.
Comment améliorer sa connexion Wi-Fi ?
Heureusement, il est possible de choisir un canal moins sollicité pour améliorer la situation. La bande 5 GHz offre plus de débit et subit moins les interférences des réseaux voisins, mais avec une portée plus faible.
Les box Wi-Fi 6E et certaines box Wi-Fi 7 proposent aussi la bande 6 GHz, encore moins encombrée. C’est la fréquence idéale pour les logements très chargés en réseaux sans fil.
Mais en revanche, la bande 6 GHz traverse moins bien les murs. À noter que certaines box Wi-Fi 7 utilisent uniquement les bandes 2,4 GHz et 5 GHz. C'est notamment le cas de la Freebox Pop Wi-Fi 7.
Si votre PC ou tout autre appareil connecté est proche de la box, vous avez donc tout intérêt à utiliser 5 GHz ou 6 GHz. Pour les objets connectés, c’est bien mieux de choisir 2,4 GHz.
Bien évidemment, il y a aussi votre propre foyer qui peut provoquer un ralentissement du Wi-Fi, notamment si plusieurs personnes en même temps regardent des films en streaming, téléchargent de gros jeux de plusieurs Go ou jouent en ligne.
Mais ce n’est pas toujours le Wi-Fi. Parfois, si le débit chute, même en Ethernet, le problème se situe au niveau de la connexion Internet. Certains réseaux d’opérateurs subissent un ralentissement de la connexion aux heures de pointe, quand beaucoup de clients se connectent.

articles.title: Une étoile morte brille en vert, et les astronomes viennent de comprendre pourquoi
articles.text:
On n’avait jamais recensé une étoile verte avant WD J1330+6435. Des astronomes de l’université de Warwick expliquent la teinte de cette naine blanche par des débris rocheux de son ancien système planétaire, tombés dans une atmosphère d’une densité hors norme.
La couleur d’une étoile dépend presque uniquement de sa température. Une étoile froide est orangée, une étoile très chaude d’un bleu pâle. Quand une étoile de la taille du Soleil épuise son combustible, elle laisse derrière elle une naine blanche, et les astronomes pensaient que ces astres morts suivaient eux aussi la règle des couleurs. Mark Hollands, chercheur en astrophysique à l’université de Warwick, a voulu vérifier cette idée avec trois collègues. Leur équipe a converti la lumière de naines blanches réparties dans tout le ciel en couleurs perçues par l’œil humain, et l’une d’elles est ressortie d’un vert chartreuse. Il faut remonter jusqu’aux restes de son ancien système planétaire pour comprendre d’où vient ce vert.
Du sodium tombé d’anciennes planètes
Les chercheurs estiment la température de surface de WD J1330+6435 à environ 4 000 °C, d’après leur étude parue mi-octobre dans la revue RAS Techniques and Instruments. Des fragments rocheux de son système planétaire sont tombés dans son atmosphère et ont apporté avec eux du sodium. C’est lui qui donne sa couleur à l’étoile. Ces débris sont récents à l’échelle astronomique, car les éléments lourds coulent vite sous la surface d’une naine blanche et disparaissent de la vue.
Dans une étoile ordinaire, le sodium absorbe une seule raie orange, très étroite. Les vieux lampadaires au sodium doivent leur teinte à cette raie. Chez les naines blanches les plus froides, la densité de l’atmosphère est d’environ un gramme par centimètre cube, autant que l’eau et des millions de fois plus que celle de la surface visible du Soleil. Dans ce plasma d’hélium très comprimé, le sodium absorbe une grande partie du jaune et de l’orange, et le calcium, lui aussi apporté par les débris, efface une part du violet. Le pic de la lumière émise est alors situé autour de 500 nanomètres, dans le vert.
« Les traces de sodium dans l’atmosphère de cette naine blanche absorbent la partie orange du spectre et laissent derrière elles une lueur verte fantomatique », a expliqué Mark Hollands. « Imaginez-vous sur une planète, en train de lever les yeux vers une étoile verte. On se croirait dans un film de science-fiction », a-t-il ajouté.
Certains titres anglophones ont fait de l’étoile un « zombie cosmique » mangeur de planètes. Selon Nature World News, l’étude montre seulement que des fragments rocheux sont tombés sur l’étoile, sans prouver que des planètes entières ont été englouties d’un seul coup.
Une couleur calculée, jamais vue à l’œil nu
Si vous pouviez vous approcher de WD J1330+6435, vous la verriez d’un vert jaunâtre. Aucune naine blanche n’est cependant assez proche de la Terre pour que sa couleur soit visible directement, et l’équipe de Mark Hollands a travaillé à partir des spectres. Dans un spectre, la lumière d’une étoile est décomposée longueur d’onde par longueur d’onde. Les chercheurs ont fait passer chacun de ces relevés dans un modèle standard de la vision humaine des couleurs, puis ont converti le résultat en valeurs affichables sur un écran d’ordinateur.
Personne n’a donc vu l’étoile briller en vert, et elle est bien trop faible pour un télescope d’amateur. Le spectre de WD J1330+6435 est assez bruité et sa teinte exacte pourrait légèrement différer, reconnaissent les chercheurs. Avec plusieurs modèles d’atmosphère, l’équipe obtient malgré tout un vert.
Les chercheurs ont aussi repéré deux naines blanches d’un vert plus pâle. WD J1011+2845, à 48 années-lumière, est d’un rose saumon profond, car la convection a fait remonter à sa surface du carbone issu de son cœur. À l’œil, elle est sans doute l’étoile la plus rouge connue.
L’équipe a ensuite passé en revue les 152 naines blanches situées à moins de 65 années-lumière de la Terre. Cinq seulement ont une teinte vraiment inhabituelle. Deux sont jaunes, trois sont roses, et les auteurs en déduisent qu’environ une naine blanche sur trente brille d’une couleur hors norme. La température de couleur médiane des 147 autres est d’environ 6 800 kelvins, soit un blanc presque pur. L’image de naines blanches bleutées est le fruit d’un biais d’observation, car les plus chaudes sont aussi les plus lumineuses et les astronomes les repèrent de plus loin dans les relevés. « Si l’on prend la médiane d’une population représentative de naines blanches, la naine blanche moyenne est vraiment blanche », a souligné Boris Gänsicke, professeur de physique à Warwick.
À environ 4 000 °C, WD J2356-2054 est elle aussi chargée de sodium, mais elle est d’un bleu vif à l’œil. D’après Mark Hollands et ses coauteurs, d’autres naines blanches d’un vert ou d’un cyan vif existent sans doute entre ces deux cas, et les astronomes pourraient les repérer dans de futurs relevés.

articles.title: PlayStation 6 Could Get Sony's Own Frame Generation Technology, Patent Suggests
articles.text:
Sunday, October 18th 2026
PlayStation 6 Could Get Sony's Own Frame Generation Technology, Patent Suggests
Sony has a new patent application that describes its own take on frame generation, and the PlayStation 6 seems like the obvious target, though no console is named. Titled "Generation Super Sampling," the filing (US 2026/0320740 A1) was published on October 15 and lists Sony engineer Denis Dupeyron as the inventor. It describes an encoder neural network that turns a newly rendered frame into a compact embedding, and a decoder network that uses it to predict the next frame. Optional inputs include motion vectors and recent controller inputs, which help the model guess where the player is heading. That frame is displayed while the next real one is still rendering.
The filing points out that existing methods insert a generated frame between two real ones, which means waiting for both and adding delay. Sony's version predicts forward from a single frame, with the goal of smoothing out hitching in heavy scenes without lowering visual quality. It can also predict several frames at once, and there's a simpler non-AI fallback that shifts blocks of pixels along their motion vectors. Apparently, the model trains on the video stream itself, comparing each guess with the real next frame, so no human labeling is needed. However, the filing includes no latency or image quality numbers, and it remains pending, so there's no guarantee any of it ships.Frame generation would be a logical next step after the PS5 Pro's PSSR upscaler, and leaks have already pointed to the PS6 targeting 4K at 120 FPS in most games. Multi-frame generation makes less sense on TVs that top out at 120 Hz, though, and some have raised concerns that developers could lean on it instead of optimizing their games. Sony has been on a roll with patents recently, with filings describing bosses that learn from your reaction times and retries, consoles that fix themselves using AI, an AI that fills in controller inputs for players with physical limitations, and even stream viewers controlling a cursor on the streamer's screen. Like those, this one is probably best treated as something Sony is exploring for now.

articles.title: Cinebench world record that stood for 12 years gets toppled — OC expert scores 10.8cb in Cinebench R11.5 using an Intel Core i5 4670K at 6.3 GHz
articles.text:
Cinebench world record that stood for 12 years gets toppled — OC expert scores 10.8cb in Cinebench R11.5 using an Intel Core i5 4670K at 6.3 GHz
Overclocking enthusiasts are still having fun with Haswell CPUs and DDR3 in 2026.
You don’t need the latest and greatest PC hardware to have fun or even break overclocking world records. OC expert Luumi has demonstrated this very capably by achieving a new HWBot world record using an ancient Intel Core i5 4670K, a modest amount of DDR3, and (inevitably) a flask or two of LN2. Overclocker Luumi recently knocked the four-cores Intel Core i5 4670K Cinebench R11.5 record holder off their perch after 12 years, achieving a multicore score of 10.8 cb.
The HWBot-crowned system is built around Haswell-era Intel silicon, the Core i5 4670K to be precise. This is an unlocked 4C/4T CPU with a stock base/boost of 3.4 / 3.8 GHz, 84W TDP, with a 6MB cache and HD 4600 graphics, built on Intel’s 22nm process. You had to buy an i7 chip back in this era to get 4C/8T.
Luumi’s system hosted the CPU on an ASRock Z97 OC Formula motherboard, which was fitted with 4GB of DDR3 RAM from XPG, and fed ample power via a Corsair AXi 1600. To achieve the Cinebench R11.5 benchmark record liquid nitrogen was used to cool the 4670K, and the validation files show the CPU ran at a blistering 6,301.00 MHz.
Again, we’ll comment that this isn’t a world record Cinebench R11.5 score for any / all quad-core processors. It's just in the Core i5 4670K category. Nevertheless, it is great to see retro hardware achievements like this, 12 years later. As one other HWBot community member commented, it is brilliant to see an OC result on the HWBot homepage that involves neither an X3D CPU or RTX 5090 GPU. You don’t need the latest, greatest, most expensive, nor unobtainuim components to get featured on the online home of competitive overclocking.
Out of curiosity I decided to give ye olde Cinebench R11.5 a spin on the laptop I’m currently working on. With its 12C/24T CPU, it trounced the old-but-record-breaking Haswell desktop, of course. Even though the laptop is running in cool/quiet mode I achieved 4x the 4670K score.
Mostly I was happy that this older version of Cinebench still works on modern hardware and Windows 11 without any fuss. Some apps which were popular benchmarking staples, like 3DMark tests from DX10 and earlier eras, have issues on modern computers making the results you can wheedle out of them invalid for HWBot rankings. Luumi used Windows 7 64-bit Pro for their Haswell CPU Cinebench R11.5 testing.

A clever developer has come up with a way to deliver lossless Dolby TrueHD movie soundtracks, complete with Dolby Atmos effects, to home theater speakers from the third-gen Apple TV 4K.
The Apple TV only officially supports Dolby Digital Plus, which is the more compressed Dolby audio codec used by streaming services to reduce the amount of data used, while Dolby TrueHD is used on Blu-rays where bandwidth isn't a problem. So it makes sense for the Apple TV 4K to only use Dolby Digital Plus, since it's a streaming device — but that doesn't stop the enthusiasts from wanting the flexibility of playing files with TrueHD audio on their devices.
The system that Reddit user Agathorpt used to deliver Dolby TrueHD through the Apple TV 4K requires not actually delivering it in TrueHD at all, but converting it to other formats, converting the Dolby Atmos positional data into other formats too, then recombining them in a format that the Apple TV 4K can deliver, but in a higher quality.
How they got TrueHD Atmos on the Apple TV 4K
As mentioned above, the audio takes a bit of a journey here. The path is:
TrueHD Atmos → decoded audio + timed object metadata → fixed 9.1.6 speaker render → APAC → native tvOS playback.
APAC is Apple's Positional Audio Codec, and while it's not truly lossless (the source audio, TrueHD, is a lossless format but APAC is not) the consensus is that the results here are really impressive.
Basically, the system decodes the audio and the 3D Atmos positioning data separately, creates a new audio system where the Atmos effects are mapped to a 9.1.6-channel speaker configuration, then converts that to Apple's own proprietary spatial audio codec, which can then be played by the Apple TV 4K.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The goal was to replicate the audio functionality of a closed-source app called Native Player with an open-source alternative because "keeping the implementation closed… leaves everyone dependent on that vendor for fixes and future support," Agathorpt says. "Other players can't reuse or improve that code, and the community can't independently inspect how it handles the audio."
"The spatial audio has been working amazingly well for me," Agathorpt says. "It sounds excellent on my setup." Other redditors have tried the same software and are reporting great results too.
In order to copy what Agathorpt has created, you'd need several things: a Mac; Apple's Xcode development software; and your own Apple development account to sign an app: the full steps they went through are detailed here. The Apple TV 4K needs to be running tvOS 26 or later, and of course you'll also need movie files with 48kHz TrueHD Atmos audio.
There is hope from home theater enthusiasts that Agathorpt's project will be implemented in the Nuvio player for everyone and in other tvOS apps too, but for now you'll need to build it yourself. It doesn't seem too difficult to do, but if you're not the technical type you might want to wait for it to roll out as part of the app. It's been proposed for addition so hopefully that won't take too long.
Agathorpt is at pains to point out that they didn't write the software projects used in this process. It builds on the work of others, especially Superuser404notfound's work on the AetherEngine media engine and LibTrueHD object audio decoder.
One assumes that this will work with the new Apple TV 4K (2026) that Apple just announced too, though its price hike and lack of big new AV features means fans aren't particularly enamored.

Her latest, a love letter to music titled Small Town Joy, is on sale now. She is the singer in spectacularly obscure Glaswegian rock band Unquiet Mind.

articles.title: Die Streaming-Falle: Bei diesen Anbietern müssen Sie trotz Abo mit Werbung rechnen
articles.text:
Streaming-Falle bei Netflix, Disney, Prime & Co.: Warum du trotz Abo plötzlich Werbung siehst
Draußen ist es schon dunkel, der Herbstwind weht, es regnet. Drinnen läuft der Filmabend bei Snacks und gedimmtem Licht. Der Detektiv ist gerade dabei, den Mörder zu entlarven. „Der Täter ist …“ Schnitt. „Ralf Schumacher?!“ Das ist natürlich überspitzt dargestellt, dürfte aber für viele deutsche Streaming-Nutzer ein Stück weit zur Realität gehören. Denn laut einer Statista-Umfrage unter 4.781 Personen zwischen 18 und 64 Jahren nutzten 51 Prozent der Befragten zwischen Juni 2025 und Juni 2026 kostenlose und werbefinanzierte Streaming-Dienste, 46 Prozent zahlen für Angebote mit Werbung wie etwa Netflix.
Zwar waren mehrfache Angaben möglich und die Daten deuten laut dem Statistikdienst darauf hin, dass viele Streaming-Fans „mehrere Streamingabos abgeschlossen haben und dabei werbefinanzierte und werbefreie Angebote mischen“. (Schließlich gaben 41 Prozent an, für Angebote ohne Reklame zu zahlen.) Die Umfrage zeigt aber deutlich, dass Werbung mittlerweile für viele zum Erlebnis dazugehört.
Günstiger Einstieg ins Streaming nur mit Werbung
Bei der Strategie einzelner Anbieter verwundert das nicht. So kostet das Netflix-Standardabo mittlerweile 15,99 Euro im Monat. Zum Start in Deutschland 2014 waren es noch 8,99 Euro. Da wirkt der Abschluss des Werbeangebots wie der logische Schluss. Auf dem Papier gleichen sich die Leistungen schließlich. Streaming in Full-HD auf zwei Geräten gleichzeitig, Downloads sind möglich. Nur kostet das Werbeabo eben nur 6,99 Euro im Monat.
Andersherum läuft es bei Amazon Prime Video. Dort läuft seit Februar 2024 Werbung vor und zwischen Filmen und Serien – grundsätzlich für alle. Wer die Anzeigen nicht sehen will, kann sie für drei Euro monatlich abschalten. Auf die eine oder andere Weise haben fast alle großen Anbieter mittlerweile Werbeabos eingeführt. Sie sehen darin offenbar lukrative Wege, um mehr Einnahmen zu generieren. Doch dabei bleibt es nicht. Bei manchen Diensten gibt es auch in teureren Abo-Varianten Anzeigen zu sehen.
Netflix
Netflix gilt als einer der Pioniere für werbefinanziertes Streaming. Zum Start des sogenannten „Standard-Abos mit Werbung“ war die Rede davon, dass es pro Stunde Streaming vier bis fünf Minuten Reklame zu sehen geben soll. Allerdings hat das Unternehmen bei der Abo-Option in den vergangenen Jahren nachgedreht. Anders als in der Ankündigung beschrieben, sind Downloads mittlerweile (eingeschränkt) möglich, die Auflösung liegt jetzt bei Full-HD, nicht mehr bei HD.
Wie viel Werbung es heute zu sehen gibt, lässt sich pauschal nicht sagen. Das Unternehmen spricht nur noch von wenigen kurzen Unterbrechungen. Diese sollen immerhin nach Möglichkeit so gelegt werden, dass sie wichtige Szenen nicht unterbrechen. Bei manchen kürzlich veröffentlichten Filmen soll die Reklame nur vor Beginn der eigentlichen Wiedergabe gezeigt werden. Komplett ausgenommen davon sind Videospiele und Titel im Kinderprofil.
Disney Plus
Auch Disney Plus bietet ein reines Werbeabo an, bei dem Anzeigen vor und während des Streamings von Inhalten laufen. Allerdings weist der Streaming-Anbieter darauf hin, dass die Optionen Standard und Premium ebenfalls „Werbeinhalte, Werbung vor oder nach der Wiedergabe von Inhalten, Clips und Trailer für Disney-Inhalte, -Produkte und -Dienste sowie Inhalte mit Branding oder Sponsoring beinhalten“ können. Die Regelung ist neu und dürfte Kunden der teureren Optionen für 10,99 und 15,99 Euro nicht zwingend erfreuen.
Amazon Prime Video
Amazon macht für seinen Dienst Prime Video deutlich weniger Angaben. „Prime-Filme und -Serien enthalten begrenzte Werbung“, schreibt das Unternehmen als einzige echte Information. Anfangs soll es bis zu drei Minuten Reklame zu sehen gegeben haben. Mittlerweile habe sich der Wert verdoppelt, schrieb Adweek mit Verweis auf interne Dokumente bereits Mitte 2025. Eine offizielle Ankündigung gab es dazu nicht. Ohne Prime-Abo kostet der Dienst 8,99 Euro im Monat oder 89,90 Euro pro Jahr. Um die Werbung abzuschalten, werden drei Euro extra monatlich fällig.
HBO Max
Seit einigen Monaten ist HBO Max in Deutschland verfügbar. Der Dienst ist direkt mit einem Werbe-Abo gestartet. Wie viel Werbung es zu sehen gibt, verrät der Anbieter allerdings nicht. „Wenn du das Basis-Abo mit Werbung hast, wird vor und während On-Demand-Serien und -Filmen Werbung abgespielt“, ist die einzige Info, die HBO Max mitgibt. Wie bei anderen Diensten lässt sich die Werbung nicht vorspulen oder ganz überspringen. Wer keine Werbung sehen will, muss mindestens 11,99 Euro im Monat für das Standard-Abo zahlen.
Paramount Plus
Bei Paramount Plus enthalten laut einer Support-Seite alle Abo-Optionen Werbung. Abonnenten sehen dann vor und nach einzelnen Titeln Trailer für die Inhalte der Streaming-Plattform. Es gibt zusätzlich ein dediziertes Basic-Abo mit Werbeunterbrechungen in laufenden Filmen und Serien. Auch Paramount Plus nennt keine genaue Minutenanzahl für Reklame pro Streaming-Stunde. Auf Plattformen wie Reddit beschweren sich Nutzer aber schon jahrelang über zu viel Werbung. Eine Auswertung von Ampere Analysis, über die Business Insider berichtet, kommt zum Schluss, dass der Dienst in den USA neun Minuten Werbung pro Stunde zeigt. Mit dem deutschen Angebot ist das jedoch nicht vergleichbar.
RTL Plus
Bei RTL Plus gibt es in zwei von drei Abo-Optionen Werbung zu sehen. Wie viele Minuten genau pro Stunde verrät das Unternehmen nicht. Die Anzeigen laufen jeweils vor und während der abgespielten Inhalte. Beim Premium-Abo sollen sie jedoch „deutlich weniger“ zu sehen sein als beim günstigeren RTL Plus Basic, informiert der Sender auf einer Übersichtsseite. Auf der Auswahlseite für die Abos gibt der Anbieter zudem noch an, im Basic-Plan werde die Reklame „regelmäßig“ eingespielt. Wie der Name schon sagt, könnt ihr den Anzeigen mit der Option „Premium Werbefrei“ aus dem Weg gehen. Der Zugang kostet 12,99 Euro im Monat.
Apple TV Plus
Als einziger großer Streaming-Dienst verzichtet Apple TV Plus auf ein eigenes Werbe-Abo. Ein wenig Reklame gibt es trotzdem zu sehen. Vor Wiedergabe der Inhalte zeigt Apple Trailer, die auf Filme und Serien im eigenen Angebot hinweisen. Diese lassen sich aber auch überspringen. Auf der eigenen Webseite beschreibt das iPhone-Unternehmen seinen Dienst als werbefrei – abgesehen von den Werbeblöcken bei der Übertragung von Live-Sport-Events.
Als Kunde von Werbe-Abos Werbung umgehen
In vielen Fällen lassen sich Anzeigen trotz eines gebuchten Werbe-Abos auf zwei Wegen umgehen. Dafür muss man allerdings Einschnitte in Kauf nehmen. So wird in Kinderprofilen in der Regel keine Werbung ausgespielt. Diese bieten aber natürlich keinen Zugriff auf Blockbuster. Möglichkeit zwei ist der Download der Inhalte aufs Smartphone oder Tablet. Das ist oft aber nur eingeschränkt möglich. Im Werbe-Abo von Netflix darf man pro Monat nur 15 Titel herunterladen. Disney Plus bietet in der günstigen Option gar keine Möglichkeit zum Download an. Auf Smart-TVs fehlt die Funktion logischerweise.

articles.title: Health, inclusion, computing: Test your business creativity with Edition 254 of our weekly quiz!
articles.text:
Health, inclusion, computing: Test your business creativity with Edition 254 of our weekly quiz!
This insightful feature from YourStory tests and strengthens your business acumen! Here are 5 questions to kick off this 254th quiz. Ready?
Lateral Sparks, the weekly quiz from YourStory, tests your domain knowledge, business acumen, and lateral thinking skills (see the previous edition here). In this 254th edition of the quiz, we present issues tackled by real-life entrepreneurs in their startup journeys.
What would you do if you were in their shoes? At the end of the quiz, you will find out what the entrepreneurs and innovators themselves actually did. Would you do things differently?
Check out YourStory’s Book Review section as well, with takeaways from over 355 titles on creativity and entrepreneurship, and our weekend PhotoSparks section on creativity in the arts.
Q1: Home appliances
Many consumers want kitchen products that are technologically advanced but designed around how Indian households cook. How can this opportunity be tapped?
Q2: Healthcare
Patients in remote villages who are under risk of heart attack face acute challenges in getting access to healthcare facilities. How can technology help here?
Q3: Financial inclusion
Many qualified but underserved entrepreneurs suffer challenges in getting access to financial resources. Where is the business opportunity here?
Q4: Advanced computing
Fields like drug discovery, materials science, manufacturing, logistics, and finance could do with computing resources that are far more powerful than currently available options. Where is the entrepreneurial opportunity here?
Q5: Personal care
The personal care market is evolving rapdily, with consumers seeking all-natural products they can trust for the whole family. How can this opportunity be tapped?
Answers!
Congratulations on having come this far! But there’s more to come – answers to these five questions (below), as well as links to articles with more details on the entrepreneurs’ solutions. Happy reading, happy learning – and happy creating!
A1: Home appliances
Founded by Eshwar K Vikas and Rakesh Patil, Beyond Appliances has conducted extensive research with Indian consumers. It has identified everyday challenges in Indian kitchens and translated those insights into unique products.
It has an omnichannel strategy with a retail presence in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad, and a manufacturing facility in Bengaluru. Read more here about its products such as Android chimneys, Plug-N-Play chimneys, smart hobs, and cooktops.
A2: Healthcare
Founded by Rajat Jain, Arpit Jain, Sabit Rawat, Nitin Chandola and Saurabh Badola, Spandan helps address gaps in timely cardiac assessment. Its devices reduce the care time after a heart attack, in private clinics, homes, and public-health systems.
It uses a smartphone to help detect a suspected heart attack, with results reviewed by remote doctors around the clock. Read more here about how frontline health workers capture an ECG using its platform for remote interpretation, and how around 60,000 devices have already been deployed.
A3: Financial inclusion
Founded by Dhruv Khaitan and Piyush Khaitan, MSME-focused digital lender NeoGrowth has developed a range of lending services. They include underwriting, portfolio monitoring, and risk management powered by proprietary AI.
It manages assets under management close to Rs 2,000 crore and has disbursed more than Rs 16,000 crore. Read more here about how it has raised a Rs 85 crore investment led by Dutch entrepreneurial development bank FMO.
A4: Advanced computing
Founded by Nagendra Nagaraja, QpiAI develops vertically-integrated quantum systems and AI platforms. They are used in areas such as drug discovery, materials science, manufacturing, logistics, and finance.
It has unveiled a 64-qubit processor, and aims to move quantum technology beyond experimentation and towards commercial use. Read more here about its recent fundraise from YourNest, SIDBI Venture Capital, Avataar Ventures, and the National Quantum Mission.
A5: Personal care
Founded by Swagatika Das and Gaurav Agarwal, Nat Habit is a an ayurvedic personal care brand. Its portfolio ranges across hair care, skin care, body care and baby care.
It combines traditional Ayurvedic principles with modern science through in-house R&D and manufacturing capabilities. Read more here about its fundraise from Trident Growth Partners, Bertelsmann India Investments, and Mirabilis Investment Trust.
YourStory has also published the pocketbook ‘Proverbs and Quotes for Entrepreneurs: A World of Inspiration for Startups’ as a creative and motivational guide for innovators.

articles.title: Sonos Ace Ultra : le transfert audio des enceintes au casque est-il vraiment utile ? On l’a testé
articles.text:
Sonos Ace Ultra : le transfert audio des enceintes au casque est-il vraiment utile ? On l’a testé
Avec l’Ace Ultra, Sonos renforce l’intégration de son casque à son écosystème grâce au transfert audio entre les enceintes et le casque. Une nouveauté attrayante pour les férus de la marque, mais qui reste pour l’heure limitée.
L’un des principaux atouts de Sonos réside dans l’interopérabilité entre ses produits. On peut ainsi s’équiper de plusieurs enceintes pour diffuser un même contenu ou des contenus différents dans les pièces de la maison, créer des paires stéréo, mais aussi faire évoluer une barre de son Sonos en lui associant des enceintes satellites sans fil.
La marque américaine s’est lancée sur le marché des casques Bluetooth il y a maintenant deux ans avec l’Ace, mais il manquait à ce premier modèle une fonctionnalité permettant de l’intégrer pleinement à l’écosystème Sonos, notamment pour convaincre les aficionados de la marque, déjà bien équipés.
Sonos Ace Ultra
L'Ace Ultra, version modernisée de l’Ace premier du nom récemment lancée, entend combler cette lacune. L’utilisateur peut désormais transférer la musique diffusée sur le système audio du foyer vers le casque. De plus, grâce à sa nouvelle puce Headphone Engine 2, l’Ace Ultra se comporte désormais comme un élément à part entière de l’écosystème domestique. Après l’avoir sélectionné dans l’app Sonos, il est donc possible de simplement streamer de la musique en Wi-Fi sur le casque depuis son service de streaming préféré.
Un transfert du système au casque simple à configurer
La configuration du transfert audio vers l’Ace Ultra est très simple. Il suffit en effet d’associer le casque au système via une option disponible dans l’application Sonos, une opération qui ne prend que quelques secondes.
Une fois le casque prêt, le transfert s’effectue en maintenant son curseur cliquable enfoncé lorsque de la musique est diffusée dans la maison ou sur un produit en particulier, et ce, même lorsque le smartphone n’est pas à portée. Confirmé par des alertes tonales bien pensées, le basculement fonctionne à tous les coups, à condition d’avoir mis en pause manuellement une lecture en Bluetooth ou une diffusion précédente via Wi-Fi.
Des limites qui compliquent l’utilisation
C’est à peu près là que s’arrête l’expérience, car plusieurs limitations viennent largement tempérer l’enthousiasme. D’une part, le casque n’étant pas compatible avec Spotify Connect, AirPlay 2, etc., le transfert ne fonctionne que lorsque la musique est diffusée via le protocole propriétaire de Sonos, c’est-à-dire directement depuis l’application. Les possibilités sont donc limitées, ne serait-ce que pour cette raison.
Par ailleurs, Sonos promet un basculement fluide, sans avoir besoin du smartphone. Dans les faits, il faut pourtant resélectionner l’Ace Ultra dans l’application pour continuer à contrôler la lecture. En effet, si l’on change de titre, le système interprète ce changement comme un nouveau flux et relance la lecture sur les enceintes. Pas très pratique, donc.
Une fois la lecture reprise et son contrôle rétabli, il devient impossible de renvoyer le son vers les enceintes par un nouvel appui long. Pour ce faire, il ne faut pas intervenir dans l’application, et l’opération s’effectue alors avec une certaine fluidité. Néanmoins, l’audio est renvoyé de manière aléatoire vers un seul appareil, même si l’ensemble de la maison diffusait le même contenu avant le premier basculement. Une curiosité de plus.
À noter que, si le casque peut être géré manuellement dans l’application Sonos et diffuser un flux différent de celui du système, il ne s’intègre pas au système multiroom. On ne peut donc pas le synchroniser avec des enceintes ou des barres de son au sein d’un même groupe.
Une continuité d’écoute encore perfectible
Au-delà de l’utilisation du casque à la maison, cette fonctionnalité semble pratique pour transférer l’audio vers le casque lorsqu’on quitte son domicile, puis vers les enceintes lorsqu’on rentre chez soi. Le premier cas de figure fonctionne bien, mais pendant quelques minutes seulement, puisqu’il est nécessaire de repasser à une connexion Bluetooth classique dès lors que le réseau Wi-Fi est hors de portée.
Lorsqu’on rentre chez soi, le réseau est détecté avant même de passer la porte, mais l’app ne conserve pas en mémoire le flux transféré avant le départ une fois la connexion Wi-Fi perdue. Il est donc nécessaire de relancer la musique sur le système audio de la maison, puis de la transférer à nouveau vers le casque.
Au regard de toutes les limitations précédemment citées, on peut en conclure que cette fonction de basculement est assez gadget et limitée. Elle fonctionne bien dans le sens des enceintes vers le casque, mais oblige malgré tout à manipuler le smartphone pour poursuivre la lecture, sans compter l’incompatibilité avec Spotify Connect, l’une des méthodes de streaming les plus largement utilisées.
